entityDescription:
AquaGuard Technologies AB (AGT) is a Swedish dual use deep tech company developing NEXUS, its proprietary AI enabled operational intelligence platform for Civil, Security and Defence applications. With a primary specialisation in the maritime domain, AGT addresses the technically challenging detection, classification, monitoring, tracking and identification of small and non cooperative vessels, including vessels operating without AIS, MMSI or other RF based identification. NEXUS combines AGT's proprietary software, AI/ML models, algorithms, processing pipelines, Multi Source Fusion and Correlation, Decision Intelligence, system architecture and operational workflows to transform fragmented observations into decision ready operational intelligence.
AGT has developed and validated AI/ML capability for precise small vessel detection and classification from high resolution satellite data, generating confidence, geolocation and associated object information independently of cooperative vessel transmissions. High resolution Optical and SAR provide complementary sensing capabilities, enabling observations from different acquisition times and conditions to be correlated within NEXUS. This extends vessel detection, classification and monitoring beyond the limitations of individual sensors and conventional cooperative tracking systems.
NEXUS brings together three complementary intelligence pillars: Space Data from high resolution Optical and SAR sources; Ground Edge AI from UAVs, USVs, fixed sensors and other local assets; and Ancillary and Contextual Data including AIS, historical records, weather, OSINT, infrastructure and partner data. Multi Source Fusion and Correlation associates these observations through entity resolution, spatial and temporal correlation, track association, confidence fusion and contextual enrichment. Decision Intelligence converts the resulting operational picture into confidence and risk assessments, anomaly and pattern analysis, operational alerts and decision support.
The same architecture supports persistent object association and cross modal vessel Re Identification (ReID), allowing observations across different times, locations and sensing modalities to contribute to an evolving digital identity and history for each vessel. Where AIS, MMSI or other identifying information is available, it can be correlated with that identity; where conventional identifiers are absent, NEXUS can maintain the observed vessel intelligence independently. This creates a pathway for persistent monitoring and identification of small and non cooperative vessels across multiple observations and sensing sources.
NEXUS is modular, sensor agnostic and interoperable, enabling additional sensors, data sources, AI models and intelligence functions to be incorporated within the same operational environment. Secure dashboards, APIs and structured geospatial outputs support direct use of NEXUS intelligence and integration with existing operational, GIS and command environments. The platform is designed to deliver timely intelligence to operational and regulatory users, with near real time capability where source acquisition and data availability permit.
NEXUS supports Civil applications including maritime safety, environmental monitoring and compliance, critical infrastructure, energy and emergency response; Security applications including maritime, border, coastal and critical infrastructure security; and Defence applications including ISR, maritime domain awareness, force protection and defence asset monitoring. The current NEXUS beta platform is deployed on AWS at TRL 6 and is progressing toward TRL 7 through continued system integration and representative operational validation.

Taranis develops a dedicated Molniya‑orbit constellation that delivers persistent polar coverage and merges optical/IR imaging with communications relay. By integrating connectivity, data and transport into a single system, we bring fiber‑like service to the world’s most underserved regions.
Conventional geostationary satellites cannot see above ~55–60° latitude, and current LEO constellations require hundreds of spacecraft to provide only intermittent coverage. Our platform uses highly elliptical Molniya orbits to maintain high elevation angles and an eight‑hour dwell over the Arctic and Antarctic, offering reliable connectivity and precise observations where infrastructure is lacking.
Through vertical integration we monetize three layers of value: connectivity – delivering broadband and IoT services at high latitudes; data – high‑quality imagery and analytics in near real‑time; and transport – reliable relay of observation data directly to users. The result is an exceptionally capital‑efficient solution designed for aviation, maritime, energy, research and government sectors.

StormGeo is a global provider of advanced weather intelligence and decision-support solutions for shipping, energy and weather-sensitive industries. Founded in Bergen, Norway, in 1998 and part of Alfa Laval, we transform complex environmental data into actionable insights that help organizations improve safety, operational efficiency and resilience.

Our capabilities include the ingestion and fusion of Earth-observation data, satellite and radar imagery, meteorological and ocean models, in-situ observations and customer asset data. We apply remote sensing, geospatial analytics, AI and machine learning to deliver site-specific forecasts, hazard monitoring, maritime and offshore decision support, energy-market intelligence, and infrastructure-risk services. Solutions are delivered through scalable cloud platforms, APIs, operational dashboards and automated alerts, supported by meteorologists and domain experts operating 24/7/365.

StormGeo processes more than 15 TB of data per day and delivers over 10 million forecasts annually across approximately 68,000 locations. Our services support thousands of offshore sites and vessels worldwide.

StormGeo was the prime contractor for GridEyeS, an ESA Business Applications project integrating Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, commercial high-resolution imagery, AI-based analytics and meteorological intelligence. GridEyeS demonstrated scalable vegetation monitoring, change detection, infrastructure-risk assessment and emergency-response support for electricity transmission and distribution networks. The service was validated with grid operators and developed into a commercially available operational solution.

We welcome collaboration with satellite and Earth-observation data providers, geospatial and AI technology partners, research organizations, infrastructure operators and downstream service providers. We are particularly interested in partnerships that turn space-derived data into scalable operational services for energy, maritime operations, critical infrastructure and climate resilience.

For 45 years, Stichting De Noordzee (The North Sea Foundation) has been committed to protecting the largest natural area of the Netherlands: the North Sea. We stand for a clean and healthy North Sea that is used sustainably. We work towards a healthy ecosystem that is resilient and adapts to external influences. North Sea nature must always be the foundation for sustainable use. We advocate for the North Sea and collaborate with other stakeholders to find solutions for current and future challenges.

Three core roles are central to our work
- Agendasetting of pressing issues and solutions;
- Collaboration within the (international) level playing field;
- Accelerating the research – policy interface
We bring these roles into practice by partnering with policymakers, (energy) sectors and operators, funders, the scientific community, and by reaching out to the general public. Our key influence lies in firmly anchored North Sea marine, spatial and nature protection policies and regulation – based on the latest scientific insights. Therefore we actively focus on national and international policy advocacy and communication. Since pressing issues do cross borders, we focus on the North Sea Basin level, stressing the importance of international marine policy cooperation and regulation. 
To realize our mission, we work on four core strategic themes: nature protection, sustainable fisheries, nature-friendly energy, and a clean sea. The nature protection program aims to safeguard large areas of the sea from human activity, allowing species space to recover – free from disturbance. In connection with this, we promote sustainable fishing practices and improved ecosystem-based fisheries management. The nature-friendly energy program is based on the idea that the North Sea is central to the energy transition, and the sustainable energy transition at sea must mitigate environmental risks and ensure nature protection and enhancement. Finally, a healthy North Sea is a clean sea – free from visible and invisible marine litter.

Prepared International (PPI) specializes in consultancy, research and training services in the field of Disaster Risk Reduction, Preparedness and Resilience, in order to inform political decision-making and to provide effective capacity-building strategies in the long term. The PPI approach encompasses a holistic set of tools for approaching Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), including the development of preparedness models, organizational development and restructuring, self-adaptive systems, and strategies for governance and mass evacuation. 
As guiding mission PPI seeks to offer detailed, specialized expertise in the field of Disaster Management to design strategies for resilience that are both practical and detailed. This includes Operational Continuity Management for urban areas, developing and mature economies, strategies for high-risk zones, and cooperation in Disaster Risk Management for conflicting communities, including in post-conflict regions. PPI also offers long-standing expertise in simulation design and capacity-building strategies. Our team of international and local experts works towards applying lessons gathered at the forefront while developing and implementing new concepts and tools, such as the new concept of United Nations Disaster Assessment and Coordination (UNDAC) Disaster Response Preparedness Missions, the development and implementation of the mission methodology for Mass Evacuations in Natural Disasters (MEND) Preparedness Missions, or the application of the stress-test methodology. Our long-standing experience in capacity assessments and investment planning was developed in missions for the UNDAC Disaster Preparedness System, UNDP, EU or national systems; therefore, systemic Emergency and Preparedness assessment methodologies like the World Bank’s Ready to Response (R2R) concept fits perfectly in our portfolio and services. In 2020, PPI developed a methodology to analyze the ability of a EP&R system to fight pandemics based on the R2R methodology.
Our experience features a strong regional focus on the Western Balkans, with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) as a point of reference both during assessments and in our recommendations for future development. In addition, PPI is part of the Advisory Group to the Disaster Preparedness and Prevention Initiative (DPPI SEE), which offers valuable knowledge on the broader region. The team suggested for this assignment consists of recognized international experts and a leading country expert. Their valuable experience will facilitate an effective and efficient assessment process, build on best practices and lead to concise recommendations tailored to the needs of Ukraine.
On top of our first-class regional and country expertise, a clear advantage of PPI is its recent experience in applying the R2R Diagnostic methodology to assess the Emergency Preparedness and Response systems of Cabo Verde and six Western Balkan states resulting in PPI experts having detailed and updated knowledge on how to implement similar tools and conduct investment planning. The fact that all countries were very pleased with the diagnostic results and recommendations made by PPI is a clear indication of the company´s ability and capacities to deliver similar assignments to the satisfaction of all stakeholders involved.
While the organization is registered under German law in the State of Bavaria (HRB 27352), the highly experienced staff is multi-national and include key local experts. All our colleagues are driven by the same understanding, namely that stronger preparedness of communities and societies is possible with the current investments in this field. In 2023, PPI received as first private organization the Special Recognition of the Averted Disaster Award, and in 2024, no less than 11 PPI colleagues received the UN Heroes Award.

Calsens is a Spanish engineering company specializing in structural monitoring and optical sensor technology. Based in Spain, they provide 24/7 online monitoring services for civil and industrial structures, combining advanced sensor hardware with their own proprietary IoT software platform.
Their work falls across three main areas:
Structural Health Monitoring — Calsens deploys optical sensors to monitor the condition of infrastructure ranging from bridges and viaducts to pedestrian walkways. Monitoring can be short-term (a few hours, for a specific test) or permanent (continuous data collection and analysis over multiple years), supporting predictive maintenance of critical infrastructure.
Optical Sensor Development — The company designs and manufactures optical sensors for a wide range of applications, including FBG (Fibre Bragg Grating) sensors for strain measurement in civil engineering, high-temperature sensors for aerospace environments, pressure sensors for pressurized conduits, and pH sensors for concrete structures. R&D is central to their identity, with the team active in both academic and private research.
Load Testing & Structural Assessment — Calsens carries out static and dynamic load tests on civil and industrial structures, complemented by finite element numerical modelling, structural fitness reports, and engineering calculations.
Their portfolio includes projects on multiple bridges and viaducts across Spain (such as the Mascarat Bridge, Viaducto Las Rosas, Viaducto Río Algar, and others), and they collaborate with a range of companies and institutions across different sectors.
